newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bank association head sees economy improving.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bank association head sees economy improving.

text.p: The head of the Swiss Bankers Association said Switzerland's economic growth should improve slowly this year thanks to low inflation, easy money and the weakness of the Swiss franc.
"There is some light at the end of the tunnel, but it's not very bright," Georg Krayer said late on Thursday night during a dinner hosted by his association for reporters.
"We have easy money and the changing price of the Swiss franc. This is helping a lot. The tourism sector is happy and so is the machinery industry."
Krayer said the 1997 inflation was likely to remain low -- projected at an annual one percent by the Swiss National Bank .
"The pressure of worldwide competition and open borders is keeping inflation low," he said.
He forecast a real gross domestic product growth rate of 0.5 percent in 1997, the same as the forecast by the Swiss National Bank and compared with a 0.7 percent contraction in 1996.
